goal: Lets IPC clients cancel blocking mining calls (waitNext, createNewBlock, waitTipChanged) using capnp's native cancellation instead of a separate interrupt() RPC.
Simplifies and speeds up cancellation for rust, python and C++ IPC clients of the mining interface.

result.summary: This PR replaces the interrupt()/interruptWait() cancellation mechanism for blocking Mining interface methods (waitTipChanged, createNewBlock, BlockTemplate::waitNext) with an optional CancelArg parameter that registers a callback run on cancellation. It leans on new request-cancellation support being added upstream in libmultiprocess (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#342), updates the capnp schema with new annotations (extraParam, allowCancellation), and updates tests (miner_tests, interface_ipc_mining.py, ipc_tests) to exercise the new mechanism.
result.problem: IPC clients of the mining interface currently need a separate interrupt() RPC call to cancel a blocking waitNext/createNewBlock/waitTipChanged call, which is less efficient and more complex than using capnp's native per-request cancellation. This affects anyone building external mining software (e.g. Stratum v2 template providers) or other multiprocess consumers who need to cancel in-flight calls.

result.card: This PR replaces the interrupt()/interruptWait() mechanism for canceling blocking Mining IPC calls (waitTipChanged, createNewBlock, BlockTemplate::waitNext) with a CancelArg/CancelGuard argument that uses capnp's native request cancellation, building on an unmerged libmultiprocess PR (#342). ryanofsky, the sole reviewer, called it 'a very nice end-to-end implementation' that makes cancellation simpler and more efficient for IPC clients, with no objections raised. The PR is a draft, CI is currently failing, and the author states only the last commit is the real change since the first is a temporary subtree bump pending the upstream PR merging, so review of the current diff may be partially invalidated once that lands. Impact is mainly leverage: it removes a workaround (separate interrupt RPCs) and could enable finer-grained cancellation for future IPC mining consumers, but it does not fix a reported bug or urgent user pain.
